builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
summary: Replaces manual parameter-count-based pruning and heuristic model resizing with automated, hardware-aware differentiable architecture search guided by serving-engine cost models. Requires integration with specific serving engines and hardware profiling infrastructure, plus computational resources for the search phase that likely exceed a single 24GB GPU for large models. Post-adoption risks include dependency on proprietary cost models that may not generalize to different hardware or engine versions, and the method may be inaccessible without the authors' specific infrastructure.
rationale: The framework requires integration with specific serving engines and differentiable search infrastructure that likely exceeds a single 24GB GPU budget, and may rely on proprietary cost models or tools not yet publicly available for reproduction.
technique: Hardware-guided differentiable architecture search for LLM pruning

claims.statement: Replaces manual parameter-count-based pruning and heuristic model resizing with automated, hardware-aware differentiable architecture search guided by serving-engine cost models. Requires integration with specific serving engines and hardware profiling infrastructure, plus computational resources for the search phase that likely exceed a single 24GB GPU for large models. Post-adoption risks include dependency on proprietary cost models that may not generalize to different hardware or engine versions, and the method may be inaccessible without the authors' specific infrastructure.

Improves average accuracy across eight benchmarks by 6.57, 2.35, and 0.57 percentage points over Minitron on RTX 5070, RTX 5080, and H100 respectively; compresses Nemotron 3.5 Super from 120B to 74B for single-B200 serving at 128K context while retaining 95% of mean benchmark score.
